headline: High: gpt-researcher can read local documents and browse with broad egress, creating default data-leak and cascading-error risk when paired with the non-networked ai-engineering-hub.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no documented input bridge, but B can read files and browse, and its MCP/file surfaces can ingest content that may be treated as instructions. Because A is docs-only and B is runnable, the interaction is inferred rather than observed; uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF A's outputs are copied into B's file or MCP inputs, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF B parses retrieved documents as instructions without provenance checks, attacker text can steer execution.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted documents into B.
Add a provenance banner to all A-generated text before B consumes it.
Require manual review before B executes any instruction-like content.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in B.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches local documents, citations, and secrets and has broad network egress; A is non-networked, so the main leakage path is B exporting sensitive workspace content to third parties. The pair shares no explicit workspace, but B's documented file and API surfaces make leakage plausible in default research workflows.
conditions: IF B is given local documents containing sensitive data, it can transmit derived content to external APIs.
IF A is used to generate content that is then stored in B's workspace, B may upload it during research.
mitigations: Restrict B to redacted inputs only.
Remove secrets from B's runtime environment before launch.
Disable external API calls for sensitive runs.
Use a separate workspace for B's documents.
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists and DLP scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no documented write or network surfaces, while B can read files, spawn subprocesses, and install packages. There is no shared writable target or locking primitive documented, so direct capability conflict is limited; uncertainty remains because A is unverified and B supports multiple instances.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory, B can overwrite artifacts A expects to remain stable.
IF B runs multiple instances against one workspace, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Use separate directories for A and B.
Run only one B instance per workspace.
Make shared outputs read-only.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B's planner/execution/publisher flow can treat upstream content as authoritative, and A can generate AI-engineering content that B may summarize or publish. No verification step is documented between them, so A's output can cascade into B's downstream actions; this is more than low because B has publishing and API reach.
conditions: IF A-generated text is fed into B's planner or publisher, B may propagate errors without independent verification.
IF B is configured to publish research outputs, mistaken claims from A can reach external consumers.
mitigations: Require source verification before B publishes.
Mark A output as untrusted input in B.
Add a human approval step for any outward-facing report.
Limit B to draft-only mode for paired runs.
requires-engineering: implement citation and claim validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: B handles local documents, citations, and multiple external APIs, while A is an open-source docs-only project with no data classes touched. The compliance risk is mainly B's retention and residency exposure for document content and API metadata; A is not cited for a separate residency issue because none is documented.
conditions: IF EU personal data is placed into B and sent to external APIs, residency or DPA obligations may be triggered.
IF sensitive documents are retained in B's workspace, retention policy mismatches can occur.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data into B.
Confirm API DPAs before use.
Purge B workspaces after each run.
Store only minimized excerpts in B.
requires-engineering: add retention controls and residency routing.
